subject: Action items from discovery — reserved pool sizing, isolation tradeoffs, and risk map
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@helixthera.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Action items from discovery — reserved pool sizing, isolation tradeoffs, and risk map

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking the time today — this was a productive discovery call. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the risks/constraints you highlighted, and proposed next steps so we can move toward a Dedicated (reserved GPU) engagement that satisfies HelixThera's compliance and throughput needs.

What we heard (pain points / goals)
- PHI workload requiring tenant isolation and auditable logs (SOC2 + specific ePHI requirements).
- Target p95 inference latency for user-facing endpoint: <= 120 ms with 99.9% availability target.
- Batch/throughput: steady-state inference footprint ~250 concurrent requests (avg 600 tokens per request), with periodic peak bursts ~3–4x for nightly reprocessing.
- Cost sensitivity on per-token unit economics for large-scale batch jobs.

Key technical constraints you mentioned
- Network egress must terminate within your VPC for audit boundaries.
- On-prem data-exchange for training artifacts during onboarding (SFTP connector).
- Requirement for deterministic fallbacks: if dedicated pool is saturated, requests must be routed to a lower-cost compatible model (different family) rather than return 429s.

Our recommended initial scope (discovery -> MVP Dedicated)
1) Reserved pool sizing: recommend a 4-GPU dedicated island for initial canary (sufficient for target latency at baseline traffic), with an autoscale policy to add 2 GPUs for peak batch windows.
2) Isolation model: single-tenant pool (isolation lane) with network egress through your VPC peering + KMS-managed keys for encryption at rest.
3) SLA / SLOs: propose 99.9% uptime for the dedicated service, 95th p50/p95 latency reporting on model route. We will draft an SLA appendix for your security team.
4) Fallback strategy: implement model routing policy that fails over to a verified quantized variant in another region for read-only traffic.
5) Ops: deliver runbook (warm restart, cache priming, KV cache warming) and a canary rollout plan (5% -> 25% -> 100%).

Open questions / risks (for your team + procurement)
- Procurement cadence: when do you expect to sign a 12-month commitment versus a 3-mo pilot? This changes buffer sizing.
- Exact data retention windows and audit log retention (security prefers 7 years; we typically provide 1–3 years by default).
- Any downstream integrations (monitoring/observability) that must be in-tenant?

Attachments
- helix_requirements.xlsx (sheet: traffic_profile, security_gates) — I attached the export of the traffic profile you shared.
- sla-draft-v0.1.pdf — informal SLA appendix placeholder.

Next steps (proposed calendar)
- Tue 2025-06-17: internal sizing + ops feasibility review (Irene/Ben/Karthik) — we will produce a one-page sizing & risk heatmap.
- Wed 2025-06-18: joint call with Helix security & procurement (30–45m) to walk the SLA appendix and procurement cadence. Can you confirm 9–11am PT window?
- By Fri 2025-06-20: send a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with dates and owners + preliminary pricing tiers for 3/6/12-mo commitments.

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the Wed slot and circulate the MAP draft afterward.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@helixthera.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@vendorcloud.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Action items from discovery — reserved pool sizing, isolation tradeoffs, and risk map

Irene — thank you for the clear recap. This is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Procurement: leadership is favoring a 6-month commitment for the initial production roll (budget sign-off mid-July). Short pilot (3 weeks) preferred before full 6-month commit to validate throughput and model quality.
2) Retention: security is asking for 5 years of audit logs for access to PHI flows — is that possible via an add-on?
3) Fallback: we like the deterministic fallback idea. A critical piece is that fallback model must not use company-sensitive embeddings — can you confirm options for a smaller open model that stays within our VPC?

Wed 06/18, 9:00am PT works for us to review SLA + procurement flow. I’ll invite our security lead (Samir is coordinating our vendor checklist) and our procurement manager.

Also: can you share a cost ballpark for the 4-GPU + autoscale-to-6 configuration (monthly committed vs. pilot rates)? Even a rough delta will help procurement model.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Rao
Head of ML Ops, HelixThera
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Action items from discovery — HelixThera clarifications / procurement tempo

Irene / Ben — forwarding Priya’s clarifying points. Quick internal notes and asks: 

- Retention: 5 years for audit logs is out of the box for enterprise customers (we support long-term retention via the audit-archive add-on). Need to confirm pricing for 5-year retention.
- Fallback model requirement: running fallback within their VPC is doable if we provide a quantized small-family model container in their private deployment (no public embeddings). Ops note: we must ensure that model artifacts are stored in their KMS and that we have a pull-authorization flow for the runtime.
- Pricing ask: We should prepare 2 line-items: (A) 6-month committed price for 4 GPU island + burst to 6 for scheduled windows and (B) 3-week pilot (4 GPU, no commit) with higher unit rates. Include audit-archive as an add-on.

Action items (internal)
- Ben: can you run a rough monthly cost delta for 4 vs 6 GPUs with current q2 rack pricing and include audit-archive? Need by EOD Tue (06/17).
- Irene: draft the MAP skeleton and SLA appendix for Wed call. Include explicit owner for audit-archive signoff.
- Karthik: I’ll prep the vendor checklist responses for Helix’s security questionnaire.

We should also prepare a simplified throughput test plan for the 3-week pilot: baseline perf, burst window simulation, and failover verification.

-K
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@helixthera.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action items from discovery — reserved pool sizing, isolation tradeoffs, and risk map

Priya / Samir — thanks and great to lock the Wed 9:00am PT slot. I’ve scheduled a 45-minute call and attached the MAP draft we'll walk through.

Immediate deliverables we’ll bring to the call:
- Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft with owners and timeline (Irene/Ben/Helix leads)
- Pricing tiers: 3-week pilot vs 6-month commitment (Ben to present)
- SLA appendix v0.1 + audit-archive add-on description (Irene)
- Pilot test plan (Karthik) with throughput scenarios and failure/fallback verification steps

Parking-lot items to confirm on the call:
- 5-year audit log retention (add-on pricing & retention SLA)
- VPC egress controls for fallback model — confirm we can host the fallback without cross-tenant embedding persistence
- Procurement lead and legal contact for contract routing

If that works, expect the calendar invite in a few minutes and the MAP link in chat (Drive link in metadata). After the call we’ll produce an updated MAP and a short SOW to align on procurement lead times.

See you shortly,
Irene
